deficiencies.description: The rewrite inserts 'that is', asserting an equivalence between acetylation/deacetylation and the overall state of transcription within the cell.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: to the acetylation or deacetylation, the state of the transcription within the cell itself.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: and to acetylation or deacetylation, that is, the state of transcription within the cell itself.
deficiencies.caseForHarm: A student reading the rewrite may believe that acetylation and deacetylation are synonymous with the state of transcription itself, rather than modifications that regulate or correlate with transcription.
deficiencies.caseAgainstHarm: The lecturer uttered the phrases in immediate apposition, making 'that is' a reasonable interpretation of the speaker's clarifying thought.

deficiencies.description: The rewrite replaces the pronoun 'they' (referring to the human viruses) with 'infection', widening the cause of chronic inflammatory events from those specific viruses to infection generally.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: There are about seven different human viruses that will precipitate cancer, and they can also predispose to chronic inflammatory events that can also help to give rise to cancer.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: There are about seven different human viruses that precipitate cancer, and infection can also predispose to chronic inflammatory events, which can also help to give rise to cancer.
deficiencies.caseForHarm: A student could understand that any infection can predispose to cancer-causing chronic inflammation, whereas the lecturer explicitly attributed this to the human viruses mentioned.
deficiencies.caseAgainstHarm: The paragraph introduced infection as the overarching topic, so attributing the predisposition to infection captures the broader context intended by the lecturer.
